propositions.text: Federal Court must review specialized tribunal's credibility analysis for reasonableness per Supreme Court precedents.
propositions.quote: The logic inherent in reviewing a specialized tribunal’s analysis of a case’s credibility requires the Federal Court to examine whether reasonableness governed the specialized tribunal’s analysis in a clear, straightforward and comprehensible manner in accordance with the Supreme Court of Canada’s judgments in Dunsmuir v New Brunswick, [2008] 1 SCR 190, 2008 SCC 9 [Dunsmuir]; Alberta (Information and Privacy Commissioner) v Alberta Teachers’ Association, [2011] 3 SCR 654, 2011 SCC 61; and Newfoundland and Labrador Nurses’ Union v Newfoundland and Labrador (Treasury Board), [2011] 3 SCR 708, 2011 SCC 62.

paragraphs.summary: The court states it must review the tribunal's credibility analysis for reasonableness per Supreme Court precedents.

propositions.text: This is a judicial review application under IRPA subsection 72(1) of the RPD decision dated July 8, 2016.
propositions.quote: This is an application for judicial review under subsection 72(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c. 27 [IRPA], of a decision rendered by the Refugee Protection Division [RPD] on July 8, 2016, whereby the applicant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court states this is a judicial review application of the RPD decision under IRPA subsection 72(1).

propositions.text: Applicant is 42, Haitian citizen, Baptist, married with three children, engineering assistant, and OTREH member.
propositions.quote: The applicant, age 42, is a citizen of Haiti and a Baptist. He is married and has three children. An engineering assistant by training, he is also a member of the Organisation des techniciens pour la reconstruction d’Haïti [OTREH], an organization that meets two to three times a month to discuss certain issues in the country.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicant's personal background and OTREH membership.

propositions.text: Applicant has been a preacher since age 15, ordained in 2003, and earned theology diploma in 2015.
propositions.quote: During his testimony, the applicant stated that he has been a preacher since he was 15. In July 2003, he obtained a certificate of ordination from the Christian Church of Christ and, in 2015, he received a diploma in theology from the École biblique baptiste Berée des Gonaïves in Haiti.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the applicant's religious background and qualifications.

propositions.text: Applicant criticized police involvement in rapes and kidnappings at OTREH meeting on April 19, 2014.
propositions.quote: During an OTREH meeting on April 19, 2014, the applicant allegedly criticized police involvement in rapes and kidnappings.

propositions.text: Applicant was arrested on April 20, 2014, by two police officers and detained for 10 days, allegedly physically assaulted.
propositions.quote: On April 20, 2014, he was allegedly arrested in front of his home by two police officers and subsequently detained for ten (10) days at the police station in Gonaïves, during which time, he was allegedly physically assaulted.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges he criticized police and was arrested and assaulted in April 2014.

propositions.text: Applicant was released April 30, 2014, without reason; police threatened him at home three days later.
propositions.quote: On April 30, 2014, he was reportedly released without being given a reason. Three days after his release, two police officers allegedly came to the applicant’s home to make death threats against him.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges release without reason and subsequent police death threats at home.

propositions.text: Applicant evaded police by moving across Haitian cities for a year, continuing pastoral work at Church's request.
propositions.quote: The applicant states that, following those events, he tried to evade the police, going from one city to the next across Haiti for a year: in Cap‑Haïtien from May to July 2014; in Port‑de‑Paix from August to September 2014; on Tortuga Island in October 2014; on La Gonâve Island from November to December 2014; and in Port‑au‑Prince from January to May 2015. The applicant states that while he was hiding in those cities, he continued his work as a pastor and preacher at his Church’s request.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states he hid in various Haitian cities for a year while continuing pastoral duties.

propositions.text: Police tracked applicant in every city; he applied for US visa April 14, 2015, denied; left Haiti May 26, 2015, applied for US asylum July 23, 2015.
propositions.quote: The applicant states that the police tracked him down in every city where he hid. Thus, on April 14, 2015, he submitted a visa application for the United States, which was denied. On May 26, 2015, he left Haiti for Fort Lauderdale, in the United States, and applied for asylum on July 23, 2015.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant states police tracked him; he applied for US visa and asylum in 2015.

propositions.text: Applicant left US April 30, 2016, went to Canada, claimed refugee protection May 11, 2016; claim accepted under Safe Third Country Agreement.
propositions.quote: Having been unable to find a job, he left his home in the United States on April 30, 2016, and travelled to Fort Erie, Ontario, in Canada. He claimed refugee protection on May 11, 2016, with an officer of the Canada Border Services Agency, which accepted the claim under the Safe Third Country Agreement, given that some of the applicant’s family members lived in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant left the US, came to Canada, and claimed refugee protection accepted under the Safe Third Country Agreement.

propositions.text: RPD found applicant not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection; applicant failed to prove serious persecution risk.
propositions.quote: The RPD concluded that the applicant was not a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection because he had not discharged his burden of establishing that there is a serious possibility of persecution on one of the Convention grounds, nor did he establish, on a balance of probabilities, that he would be personally subjected to the risk of torture, threats to his life, or to cruel and unusual treatment or punishment if he were to return to Haiti.

propositions.text: RPD found credibility was determinative and applicant was not credible due to vague, unclear, contradictory testimony.
propositions.quote: According to the RPD, the determinative issue was credibility. It found that the applicant was not credible, highlighting the vague, unclear, contradictory and inconsistent nature of his testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the applicant not credible and dismissed his refugee claim for lack of proof of persecution risk.

propositions.text: RPD found applicant's testimony about police officers vague, unclear, lacking spontaneity and details.
propositions.quote: In its decision, the RPD first noted that the applicant’s testimony on questions related to the identity and misconduct of the police officers was vague and unclear. The RPD found that the applicant’s responses showed a “lack of spontaneity and details”.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found the applicant's testimony about police officers vague and lacking detail.

propositions.text: RPD noted inconsistency about arrest timing; applicant's explanation rejected as mere error.
propositions.quote: The RPD also noted certain inconsistencies between the applicant’s testimony and his statements at the Fort Erie point of entry; in particular, at the hearing, he stated that he had been arrested by police the day after an OTREH meeting, whereas at the point of entry, he stated that he had been arrested a few days after the meeting. The applicant explained that this contradiction was the result of a simple error when he was telling his story at the point of entry, an explanation that the RPD rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found inconsistency in arrest timing and rejected applicant's explanation as error.

propositions.text: RPD considered OTREH president's letter confirming applicant's membership and noted president was not hiding from authorities.
propositions.quote: The RPD took note of a letter written by the president of the OTREH on paper bearing its letterhead. The letter confirmed the applicant’s membership in the OTREH. Based on that letter, the RPD noted that the president of the organization was not hiding from the authorities and was still working in Gonaïves, which did not corroborate that other OTREH members were persecuted by the police.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD noted the OTREH president's letter and that he was not hiding, undermining persecution claims.

propositions.text: RPD found inconsistency in applicant hiding yet publicly advertising sermons; preaching locations did not match hiding places.
propositions.quote: The RPD found other inconsistencies, namely the applicant’s statement that while he hid in several cities for over a year, he publicly advertised his sermons. The RPD concluded that if the applicant was truly hiding, he would not have agreed to have his sermons publicly advertised. Furthermore, the panel concluded that the places where he was preaching did not correspond to the places where he was allegedly hiding.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found contradictions between hiding and publicly advertising sermons in different locations.

propositions.text: RPD noted applicant obtained children's birth certificates in person, contradicting claim of hiding; rejected spouse explanation.
propositions.quote: Lastly, the RPD noted the fact that the applicant went to the civil registrar in his commune to obtain his children’s birth certificates. The applicant explained to the RPD that it was his spouse, not him, who went to request the birth certificates. The RPD dismissed that explanation because the birth certificates clearly indicate that [translation] “Mr. Job Delicat” appeared and not his spouse. The RPD was of the opinion that if the applicant was truly hiding from the State, he would not have gone to the civil registrar.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD found applicant's presence obtaining birth certificates contradicted his hiding claim and rejected spouse explanation.

propositions.text: RPD concluded significant credibility problems and dismissed applicant's claim.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the RPD concluded that there were several significant problems that undermined the applicant’s credibility. Consequently, the RPD dismissed his claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD dismissed the applicant's claim due to significant credibility problems.

propositions.text: Applicant's original counsel withdrew; new counsel took case but did not submit supplementary memorandum by March 23, 2017.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the applicant, Constance Byrne, withdrew from the case because she was no longer able to reach her client. Guy Nephtali took up the case. As of March 23, 2017, he had not submitted a supplementary memorandum. The original memorandum was argued.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes counsel change and no supplementary memorandum filed by new counsel.

propositions.text: Issue is whether RPD erred in assessing applicant's credibility, a fact question reviewed for reasonableness with deference.
propositions.quote: This application for judicial review raises the issue of whether the RPD erred in assessing the applicant’s credibility. The RPD’s assessment of credibility is a question of fact that falls within the RPD’s specialized field of expertise; it requires the application of the reasonableness standard and some deference (Dunsmuir, cited above).

paragraphs.summary: The court states the issue is whether the RPD erred in credibility assessment, reviewed for reasonableness with deference.

propositions.text: Contradictions, omissions, and implausibilities create clear inconsistency in internal logic.
propositions.quote: Given the contradictions, omissions and implausabilities between the testimony and the statements at the point of entry, there is a clear inconsistency in the internal logic.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds contradictions and inconsistencies in the applicant's testimony and statements.

propositions.text: Lack of details about alleged acts supports RPD's reasonable decision; applicant's behavior inconsistent with fear of persecution.
propositions.quote: The lack of details regarding the reprehensible acts alleged by the applicant lead the Court to find that the RPD decided the case in a reasonable manner based on the evidence presented to it. The applicant’s behaviour is inconsistent with his fear of persecution.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the RPD's decision reasonable given lack of detail and inconsistent applicant behavior.

propositions.text: The application for judicial review is dismissed for key reasons.
propositions.quote: For these key reasons, the application for judicial review is dismissed.

propositions.text: The court orders that the application for judicial review is dismissed.
propositions.quote: THIS COURT ORDERS that the application for judicial review is dismissed.

propositions.text: There are no questions of general importance to be certified.
propositions.quote: There are no questions of general importance to be certified.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the application for judicial review and orders dismissal, finding no questions of general importance to certify.
